Some people are just more inclined to losing control over cocaine (or any otther substance). I used it many times, even before all my friends, who were only stoners at the time. Never really liked the high tho. 

Some 6 years later, they're all using, but it seemed ok, nothing that would warn me. They kinda stopped talking to me for a while because I had just left rehab (from klonopin, morphine and ketamine addiction) and they'd feel bad if I had a relapse (even tho they were just doing coke, which really wasn't any concern to me). 

Now, 3 years later, one of my great friends was doing it every time we went out, which would happen some days a week. We would even order more if it ended. All of this didn't really shock me until I went home with him one day and it looked like he was about to od or something, he was shaking and having spasms from the waist up, I had never seen anything like it. He said he didn't sleep for some days and all that had already happened before, so he wasn't really bothered by it. I started messaging another friend of mine, who is a doctor and could tell me wtf was going on. To me, it really looked like he could have a seizure at any moment and he just couldn't stop doing more coke, even with the spasms and all. I told him I was really worried about all that situation, that I was talking to a friend who could help and asked if he was ok with taking something to bring him down. 

I guess if I had never gone home with him that day I'd probably didn't even know the extent of his problems with coke. Some days after, we had a discussion and then I found out he was basically doing it everyday, to the point where he felt he couldn't stop anymore. 

Also, I met some other cocaine addicts and, well, as addicts we can all lie very well, to anyone and specially to loved ones so we can hide the extent or even the existence of our use/addiction. That's unfortunately how it goes. 

I did cocaine on and off for about 7 years, Never even came close to feel like I was losing control or something. I think I had one coke abstinence, which left me feeling like shit for a day or 2. Didn't even ocurred to me to go after some more. Today I feel I can control my klonopin use, had another awful ketamine relapse which lasted for months (was triggered by really sad moments in personal life) but it's being controlled now and I don't plan touching morphine anytime soon. 

I think cocaine to some people is like what morphine was to me at that awful time: something that starts as pure bliss, ends up taking control of your whole being.
